name: AutoFine
description: Existing image-text retrieval benchmarks fail to sufficiently evaluate the fine-grained semantic discrimination capabilities of multimodal pre-trained models due to limitations such as semantic sparsity in images and coarse-grained descriptions. Moreover, the high cost and poor scalability of manual annotation hinder the development of large-scale, high-quality benchmarks. To address these issues, we propose AutoFine, a fully automated approach to augment existing benchmarks via regionlevel semantic differences. This method utilizes dual-path imagetext retrieval to identify semantically similar images with finegrained regional differences. It then integrates recursive visual exploration with text generation guided by a large language model to produce fine-grained captions enriched with entity and attribute details. reputation: A recent benchmark proposal for fine-grained multimodal retrieval and understanding, with emerging but not yet broad community adoption.
notes: Non-LLM multimodal benchmark; designed to stress fine-grained semantic discrimination. As a new benchmark, public leaderboards and saturation levels are likely limited.
